key_big: Same signs → positive; different signs → negative
body_html:
How it works

Adding a negative moves left on the number line; subtracting a negative moves right: 5 − (−3) = 8.

Multiplying or dividing: if the signs are the same the answer is positive, if they are different it is negative. (−6) × (−7) = 42, (−6) × 7 = −42, 42 ÷ (−6) = −7.

(−3)² = 9, but −3² = −9 (the square comes before the minus).

Example

Work out (−8) × (−5).

Same signs: positive

Answer: 40

Example

Work out −36 ÷ 4.

Different signs: negative

Answer: −9

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a negative times a negative is negative.
  • Reading −3² as 9 (it is −9; (−3)² is 9).
  • Adding the numbers instead of multiplying them.

faq.q: Why is a negative times a negative positive?
faq.a: Multiplying by −1 reverses direction on the number line; reversing twice brings you back to the positive side.

faq.q: What are the sign rules for division?
faq.a: The same as for multiplication: same signs give a positive answer, different signs a negative one.
